# Installing GSAP in Next.js/React Projects

## Installation Method

For Next.js/React, the recommended approach is using npm:

```
npm install gsap
```

## Plugin Registration

According to the documentation, you should explicitly register plugins to prevent tree-shaking issues in production builds:

> "Modern build tools often use a process called tree shaking to remove unused code. Sometimes they are over-aggressive and drop plugins due to the fact that you didn't reference them anywhere in your own code. To prevent this, you must explicitly register the plugin(s)"

Register multiple plugins at once:
```javascript
gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTriggerPlugin, DrawSVGPlugin);
```

## Important Notes

The documentation states: **"No, it's perfectly fine"** to register plugins multiple times—it neither helps nor harms.

You can consolidate plugin imports in a central `gsap.js` file, then import from that file elsewhere to avoid duplicate registrations in modular environments.

content.text: I have enough information to compile a precise summary. Let me return the structured output.

coreAPI: gsap.to(targets, vars) - Tweens from current state to vars values. targets: string|Element|Element[]|object|object[]; vars: object with properties to animate plus special props (duration, ease, delay, onComplete, etc). Returns a Tween. Example: gsap.to('.box', { rotation: 27, x: 100, duration: 1 })
gsap.from(targets, vars) - Tweens from vars values to current state. Same signature shape as to(). Useful for 'reveal' animations where the end state is the rendered state. Returns Tween.

gsap.fromTo(targets, fromVars, toVars) - Explicit start and end values. fromVars defines initial property values; toVars defines destination values plus special props (ease, duration, delay, onComplete). Returns Tween.
gsap.set(targets, vars) - Immediately sets properties (zero-duration tween). Useful for initial state setup. Returns Tween.

gsap.timeline(vars?) - Creates a Timeline sequencing container. vars accepts callbacks (onComplete, onStart, onUpdate, onRepeat, onReverseComplete + *Params variants), delay, duration, repeat, repeatDelay, yoyo, paused, defaults (inherited tween defaults), callbackScope, smoothChildTiming, autoRemoveChildren. Chainable methods: tl.to(target, vars, position), .from(...), .fromTo(target, fromVars, toVars, position), .set(target, vars, position), .add(child, position), .call(callback, params, position). The 'position' parameter accepts absolute time, relative ('+=0.5', '-=0.2'), or label strings.

gsap.registerPlugin(...plugins) - Variadic; pass any number of plugin objects. Required to prevent tree-shaking from dropping plugins in modern bundlers. Re-registering is a no-op (harmless). Example: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, DrawSVGPlugin).
input.pluginRegistration: In a Next.js project, gsap.registerPlugin() must run only on the client because plugins like ScrollTrigger reach for window/document at module-evaluation time. Practical pattern: keep registration inside a 'use client' file, ideally inside the component body (or inside the useGSAP callback), or guard with `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')`. A common pattern is a central `lib/gsap.ts` (marked 'use client') that imports gsap + plugins and calls gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, ...) once; other client components import from that file. Per the docs: 'you must explicitly register the plugin(s)' so bundler tree-shaking does not drop them, and registering multiple times is 'perfectly fine'.
freePluginsRelevant: MotionPathPlugin - FREE (previously bundled with Club, now fully free post-Webflow)
CustomEase - FREE as of the post-Webflow free release (formerly Club GSAP)
SplitText - FREE (formerly Club GSAP / 'members-only', explicitly called out in the licensing page as now free)
MorphSVGPlugin - FREE (formerly Club GSAP, explicitly called out as now free)
InertiaPlugin - FREE (formerly Club GSAP, replaced ThrowPropsPlugin)
input.useGSAPHookPattern:
Import: `import { useGSAP } from '@gsap/react'` and optionally `gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP)` to avoid React version mismatches. Signature: `useGSAP(callback, configOrDeps?)`. The callback receives `(context, contextSafe)` and runs inside a gsap.context() so all animations/ScrollTriggers/Draggables/SplitText created during it are tracked. Scope ref: pass `{ scope: containerRef }` so every selector inside the callback (e.g. '.box') is automatically scoped to descendants of containerRef.current — no manual querying needed. Deps: pass a `dependencies` array (or an array as the 2nd arg) just like useEffect; combine with `revertOnUpdate: true` to revert on every dep change (defaults to reverting only on unmount). contextSafe: wrap any handler created AFTER the hook runs (click handlers, setTimeout callbacks) so the animations they create are still tracked and cleaned up — either via the second callback arg `(ctx, contextSafe) => { const onClick = contextSafe(() => gsap.to(...)) }` or via the destructured return `const { contextSafe } = useGSAP({ scope: ref })`. Return cleanup: return a function from the callback to remove event listeners or other side effects — GSAP animations themselves are reverted automatically, so the returned cleanup is only for non-GSAP teardown (e.g. `return () => el.removeEventListener('click', handler)`). Canonical pattern: ```const container = useRef(null); useGSAP(() => { gsap.to('.box', { rotation: 180, duration: 1 }); }, { scope: container });``` then `
`.
input.nextjsClientComponentGuidance: Per GSAP docs: 'If you're using the app router / react server components, you need to drop a use client at the top of your file for useGSAP() to work.' Concretely: (1) Mark any file that imports `gsap`, any plugin, or `useGSAP` with `'use client'` at the top — these modules touch window/document at evaluation and cannot run on the server. (2) Call `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, SplitText, ...)` only on the client; safest place is inside the component body or inside the useGSAP callback. A central client-only `lib/gsap.ts` that registers once is a clean pattern. (3) useGSAP uses an isomorphic layout effect internally — it prefers useLayoutEffect but falls back to useEffect when window is undefined, so the hook itself is SSR-safe to import, but its callback only fires on the client. (4) Cleanup is automatic when the scope ref unmounts: the underlying gsap.context() reverts every tween, ScrollTrigger, Draggable, and SplitText created during the hook. You only need to return a cleanup function for non-GSAP side effects (event listeners, observers).
